question: A trader buys two articles A and B for ₹600. He sells A at 20% profit and B at 10% loss. If he gains 8% in the whole transaction, then the cost price (in ₹) of article A is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ef7298c7e9976770f9f3f889f47942bc6e00b627965929065978c4a2fd94fc6.png] 

Cost price of A = 600 x 3/5 = Rs. 360

**∴ Cost price of A is Rs. 360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

Cost price of (A + B) = Rs. 600

A sell at profit = 20%

B sell at loss = 10%

Whole profit = 8%

**Formula used:**

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Selling price at loss = Cost price x (100 - loss%)/100

**Calculation:**

Let Cost price of A = Rs. A

Cost price of B = Rs. (600 - A)

According to the question,

A times (120)/(100) + (600 - A) times (90)/(100) = 600 times frac {108}{100}

⇒ (120A + 54000 - 90A)/(100) = 648 

⇒ 30 A + 54000 = 64800

⇒ 30A = 10800

⇒ A = 360

∴ Cost price of A is Rs. 360.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Profit = Selling price - Cost price 
 
• Profit% = [(Selling price - Cost price) × 100] ÷ Cost price
 
• Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100
 
• Loss = Cost price - Selling price
 
• Loss% = [(Cost price - Selling price) × 100] ÷ Cost price
 
• Selling price at loss = Cost price x (100 - loss%)/100
 
• Selling price at discount = Marked Price x (100 - discount%)/100
